validator: Terminal profile, native bridge, build, input, capture, contrast, and shell-ownership audit
outcome: The embedded Ghostty surface uses an audited Antiky color profile while the user keeps control of the shell, prompt, profile, font family, commands, environment, history, and coding agent.

attempts.disposition: The profile contract first failed because the Antiky resource did not exist. The audited profile and complete palette then passed.
The packaging contract first failed because Tauri had no terminal resource mapping. Exact source and bundle path tests then passed.
The bridge contract first failed because it did not validate an isolated profile or load it after user configuration. Native and Rust contracts then passed.
A cold native launch showed a white bootstrap frame. Native-window, HTML-bootstrap, AppKit-view, loading, and error backgrounds now use #08090b.
The first AppKit color assertion used the wrong Objective-C selector spelling. The corrected assertion passed against the unchanged implementation.
A test-name filter was passed through npm to Cargo with the wrong argument boundary. The complete native package command then passed.

Changing the SSPS preference raced terminal teardown and left the workspace on Opening terminal. A red lifecycle test led to one serialized close-before-reload path; packaged on-off-on checks then passed.
Command-V did not reach Ghostty. A red bridge regression led to explicit Command-C and Command-V handling while other Command shortcuts remain with AppKit; packaged paste then passed.
Computer Use did not type non-ASCII text into the native view. An ASCII-only printf fixture emitted lambda, arrow, dragon, and accented text through the real PTY and proved Unicode rendering.
The restricted sandbox denied the repository check's loopback listener. The identical npm run check passed with scoped loopback permission.
The environment denied the isolated zsh-marker launch. No alternate or indirect launch was attempted.
Computer Use denied the copied missing-profile app, and the follow-up original-bundle launch was interrupted. The exact resource was restored and its source and bundle hashes match.
The React error-shape test first failed because the formatter was not exported. The formatter and exact two-field Rust serialization then passed.

The first verifier required pre-existing app bundles before it ran build commands. It now validates declarations first, builds debug and release bundles, and then compares every packaged profile digest.

tests.evidence: 16 Node contract tests, 4 Rust unit tests, and 5 Rust integration tests passed.
TypeScript and the Vite production build passed.
The release native binary built with pinned Ghostty.

The source-development outputs and release macOS app bundle contain the same audited profile digest as source and the debug bundle.
All workspace typechecks, tests, shader builds, documentation generation, and the production website build passed with scoped loopback permission.
All current PNG and JPEG pointers and local LFS objects passed.
The native Rust source is formatted.

rollback.trigger: A white startup frame, mismatched terminal colors, unsafe profile key, lost shell ownership, duplicate terminal, input regression, or unstable profile error.
rollback.action: Create a corrective or revert commit to the last passing checkpoint and rerun the complete verifier. Do not rewrite shared history.
